title: Duty planning | Kaderblick Docs

hero.heading: Duty planning for matches and events
hero.lead: Use duty planning to assign stewarding, admission, cash desk, parking, medical service and other club duties to specific people, times and areas.

body:
Duty planning at a glance

Every duty plan belongs to a match or another calendar event. The date, venue and duty plan therefore remain connected. Open the central overview through Team & club → Duty planning. You can also find the plan directly in the event and match details.

The central overview, the Duty planning step in the event wizard and every management action are shown only to people with an active club-level Duty coordinator assignment. A coaching assignment or permission to edit an event is not sufficient.

In the overview, choose a date range and filter by All visible plans, My duties or Plans with gaps. Each entry shows the event, the plan status and, where applicable, outstanding responses or missing staff.

  • Draft: the plan is still being prepared and is visible only to active duty coordinators for the responsible club.
  • Published: assigned people can see the plan and respond to their duty.
  • Closed: the duty has ended and the plan remains as a record.

Prepare a duty plan carefully

Whenever possible, prepare the duty plan together with the event. Before entering it, establish which areas must be staffed, when people must be present and who will coordinate the work.

  1. Check the date, start time and venue of the match or event.
  2. List the required services, such as stewarding, admission, cash desk, parking and medical service.
  3. Split large tasks into clear areas, for example “Main entrance”, “Away entrance” or “North car park”.
  4. Set the start, end and required number of people for each area.
  5. Check whether a particular qualification is required.
  6. Choose a responsible person who will follow responses and changes.
ℹ️
Event time and duty time are separate
A duty may begin before the event or end afterwards. Enter the actual working time for every area.

Create or edit a duty plan

In the central overview, choose Create duty plan, find the existing match or event and then configure the complete plan. Alternatively, prepare it in the Duty planning step while creating an event. The same functions are available in the details of a saved event.

  1. Choose the responsible club. The list contains clubs you may manage.
  2. Choose the responsible person. This person receives information about responses and volunteer offers.
  3. If required, enter a response deadline and general instructions.
  4. Enable Allow volunteer offers if club members may offer themselves for suitable open duties.
  5. Choose Add duty area.
  6. Select the duty type and enter a clear area name.
  7. Enter the duty start, duty end and required staffing level.
  8. Select required qualifications and the intended people.
  9. Add instructions that apply only to this area.
  10. Add the remaining areas and save the plan.

The five prepared duty types are Stewarding, Admission, Cash desk, Parking and Medical service. A club can add further types.

⚠️
Check before saving
The duty end must be after its start. Every area needs a duty type, area name, times and at least one required person.

Publish a draft and keep it up to date

A newly saved plan initially remains a draft. Review all areas, times and assignments, then choose Publish plan. Assigned people are notified and asked to respond only after publication. In a draft, an assignment is therefore neither confirmed nor cancelled.

You can continue editing a published plan. Newly assigned people are notified. When you remove a person, the former assignment remains visible under Previous assignments as an auditable record and is marked as cancelled. Open reminders and obsolete notices for that assignment are cleared. A notification that has already been delivered remains in the notification history; opening it explains that the assignment was cancelled.

Remind outstanding responses contacts only people whose own response is still pending in a published plan. Kaderblick also sends automatic reminders before the response deadline and before the duty.

If the associated event is cancelled, Kaderblick closes the plan, cancels active assignments and informs the affected people. Deleting the complete duty plan removes open, undelivered plan-related notices and reminders. Notifications that were already delivered remain available; opening the associated event explains that the duty plan was removed. Delete a plan only when its detailed assignment and attendance records are no longer needed.

Respond to assignments and volunteer offers

An assigned person sees the duty in the calendar and event details. Only that person can choose Confirm duty or Decline duty for a pending response. A duty coordinator cannot make this personal decision on somebody else's behalf. The coordinator can remove an assignment or assign another person. An optional message can contain a question or short explanation.

If volunteer offers are enabled, suitable club members can choose Offer to help with this duty for an open area. An offer is not yet a confirmed assignment. A club duty coordinator accepts or rejects it, and the member is informed of the decision.

For areas that require qualifications, assignment and volunteering are available only when all required qualifications are valid on the event date.

Record attendance on the event day

A duty coordinator for the club can record the actual progress of confirmed assignments.

  1. Open the plan from the event or match details, or from the central overview.
  2. When a person arrives, choose Record attendance. Kaderblick stores the time.
  3. At the end, choose Record duty end.
  4. If a time was recorded accidentally, choose Reset attendance and record it again.
  5. When all work is complete, choose Close plan.

If a correction is required, reopen a closed plan with Reopen as draft. Afterwards, check whether it needs to be published again.

Print duty lists

For one event, open its plan and choose Print duty plan. For several events, select the required plans in the central overview and choose Print selected plans.

The print view opens as a landscape PDF. It contains the event, list version, responsible person, duty and area, working time, names, response status, attendance, blank rows up to the required staffing level and a signature field. Use the PDF viewer’s print command or save the file for the person in charge.

🖨️
Print the current version
Create the list again after the latest changes. A PDF that has already been saved does not update automatically.

Manage duty types, qualifications and templates

Open Club-wide settings in the central duty planning area and select the club first. The settings apply to that club.

Duty types

The five standard types are already available. You can edit their name, colour, icon and usual times relative to the event, add further duty types or deactivate types no longer used. The relative times are suggestions and can be changed in an individual plan.

Qualifications

Create evidence required for particular duties, such as a medical qualification. Then select a person, assign their qualifications and add an expiry date for time-limited evidence. Without a date, the qualification remains valid indefinitely.

Templates

Open the Templates tab and choose New template. Enter a name and optional description. For every duty area, set the duty type, a clear area name, required staffing level, start and end relative to the event time, required qualifications and notes. Choose Add duty area for additional services. Saving becomes available only when every area is complete and its time range is valid.

Existing templates can be fully edited or deactivated in the same overview. You can also use Save as template while editing a specific plan. A template does not retain people from an earlier event. When creating a new plan, select the template and choose Apply template; then check the proposed times and assign the appropriate people.

Stewards and steward book

  • Create Lead steward as a separate area with exactly one person.
  • Select an association rule and enter the expected attendance when required.
  • Kaderblick warns you if the planned staffing level is too low.
  • Add the match number, referee, assistants and special incidents.
  • Select Print steward book.

The steward book includes active internal and external stewards. Missing people appear as blank name rows. Signatures are collected on the printout.

Add external helpers

Enter people without a Kaderblick account by name. They count towards staffing and appear in attendance and printouts. They do not receive notifications.

Visibility and responsibilities

  • Duty coordinator: this club-level assignment is maintained in user and club administration. Only an active duty coordinator for the relevant club can create, edit, publish, remind, print and close plans, record attendance, and manage duty types, qualifications and templates.
  • Coach: a coaching assignment alone provides no duty-management access. The navigation entry, Create duty plan action and wizard step are therefore absent.
  • Responsible person: must be assigned as a duty coordinator for the club on the event date. Selecting somebody as responsible does not grant additional access.
  • Assigned person: sees their own assignment and can confirm or decline an outstanding request.
  • Other authorised event members: see a published plan, but not automatically the names, notes and attendance records of other people.
  • Club members: can volunteer only if volunteering is enabled, a place is free and all required qualifications are valid.

Kaderblick evaluates every management action in the backend and sends the result to the interface. Navigation, event wizard, event details and match details therefore use the same permission decision.

Common questions and safe solutions

The duty plan or a button is missing

Check the selected date range and filter. Drafts are visible only to active duty coordinators for the responsible club. For one event, also open its details. If a management action is still missing, contact the club administration.

A person cannot be selected

The list contains active, verified people who belong to the responsible club. Also check whether the area requires qualifications and whether they remain valid on the event date.

A warning symbol shows an overlap

The person has another active duty at the same time. Open both plans and change the time or assignment. The warning allows the conflict to be reviewed and resolved.

The plan remains understaffed

Compare the assigned number with the required staffing level. Assign further people or enable volunteer offers. Declined, cancelled and unaccepted volunteer offers do not count as staffed places.

A reminder reaches nobody

The manual reminder is sent only to people with an outstanding response in a published plan. Confirmed or declined assignments do not receive another request.

The printed list is out of date

Close the old PDF, open the current plan and create it again. A PDF always shows the plan as it stood when the file was created.
